what: AECOM designs infrastructure. Its engineers plan and oversee the building of roads, bridges, water systems, transit lines and environmental remediation, mostly for governments.
customers: Transport departments, water authorities, defence agencies and local governments in the United States, Britain and Australia.
money: design and programme management in North America
the same work in Britain, Australia, the Middle East and Asia
moat: Framework agreements with public agencies that run for years, and the specific experience and clearances required to bid for large public works at all.
risks: A 1.9% net margin: design services are people-heavy and low margin by nature
Revenue depends on government budgets and the pace of infrastructure appropriations
29 times earnings for a business growing slowly
opportunities: Analysts see about 20% upside, with 12 covering the stock
Having sold its construction arm, the remaining design business carries less risk and better margins
American and British infrastructure programmes are funded for several years ahead
watch: Net service revenue growth and the design backlog.
